items.title: Branford Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Mrs. Dewey, my fourth grade teacher, she loved reading Mark Twain, but she didn’t like black people

ctx.x: Are we talking about seventh grade, or are we talking about younger now?

Fourth grade, fifth grade, sixth grade, seventh grade. I mean you know, it was like this thing. Mrs. Dewey, my fourth grade teacher, she loved reading Mark Twain, but she didn’t like black people, so she would always have me read the pages with the word “nigger” on it in a class full of white people, you know.

items.title: Branford Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: There was one time that she went to the school and cursed Miss Dewey out was because, you know, she didn’t care about none of that other stuff.

ctx.x: Un-huh. Un-huh. I know your mother’s strong—Delores.
Yeah, she’s combative man, Jesus. Angry black woman there, boy. Yeah, there was always, you know…. There was one time that she went to the school and cursed Miss
Dewey out was because, you know, she didn’t care about none of that other stuff. Like she wasn’t …. We were learning plurals, or something like that, and I said fishes….
